meta.description: Estimate causal effects of an exposure on an outcome from GWAS summary statistics using genetic instruments. Implements IVW (fixed/random), MR-Egger, weighted median/mode, MR-RAPS, CAUSE, GSMR-HEIDI, MR-PRESSO, MVMR, MR-Clust, LCV, and LHC-MR via TwoSampleMR, MendelianRandomization, MR-PRESSO, cause, and lhcMR. Use when testing causal direction between traits, evaluating drug-target effects via cis-pQTL/cis-eQTL, performing multivariable mediation MR, distinguishing causation from correlated horizontal pleiotropy, or producing STROBE-MR-compliant sensitivity batteries.
meta.note: 9 inputs = the pre-fix 7 re-run as regression tests (1-7, same scenarios) plus 2 new inputs (8-9) exercising CAUSE and LCV, both newly installed in this environment and absent from the pre-fix audit.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/trial results/p-values in any of the 9 outputs. Every statistic is a value this session actually computed against real (GIANT BMI15 x PGC MDD18) or clearly-labelled synthetic data with planted ground truth; the CAUSE crash and the LCV inconclusive-gcp result are both reported as what they are, not dressed up as successes.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (personal-genotype 'should I lose weight' framing) was correctly declined, citing SKILL.md's own Decision Tree row ('n=1 is wrong regime -> Not MR') and the binary-outcome non-collapsibility caveat, unchanged from the pre-fix behavior.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found. The pre-fix P1 finding (Decision Tree overstating MR-RAPS as sufficient for one-sample-equivalent designs) is now FIXED: Input 7's regression re-run confirms MR-RAPS still does not correct sample-overlap bias (b=0.23 vs naive 0.245, true=0), and SKILL.md's Decision Tree/Operational rule text now correctly states this instead of implying MR-RAPS alone suffices.

The P1 coloc fix is also verified: the rewritten LD-tag-decay data generator in examples/cis_mr_drug_target.R now reliably clears its own PP.H4>=0.7 threshold (PP.H4=1.00, Input 2), and the P1 SIMEX fix runs cleanly using the new precomputed-weights code block (Input 5). One new, environment-level finding: CAUSE 1.2.0.335's cause() crashes inside its own in_sample_elpd_loo() step against the installed loo 2.10.1 (Input 8) -- but this is not code this Skill ships (SKILL.md gives CAUSE only as prose + a pointer to pleiotropy-detection's full example, no inline CAUSE code block here), so it does not fail this Skill's own M4 check.

Both dispatched P1 fixes are verified end to end, not just by inspection: the rewritten LD-tag-decay coloc example now reliably clears its own PP.H4>=0.7 threshold (achieved 1.00, was 0.197), and the SIMEX precomputed-weights code runs to completion without the pre-fix 'object se.outcome not found' crash.

The third P1 fix (Decision Tree/Operational rule text on MR-RAPS and sample overlap) is a documentation correction that this audit's own re-run of the same UKB-on-UKB scenario confirms is now empirically accurate: MR-RAPS still fails to correct the bias, and the text no longer implies otherwise.

The redundancy pass materially reduced SKILL.md/usage-guide.md duplication (usage-guide.md 125->78 lines) while closing a real gap in passing (SKILL.md's install block was missing 'simex' even though it now ships runnable SIMEX code).

recommendations.title: CAUSE crashes inside its own ELPD model comparison against the installed loo version
recommendations.problem: Following SKILL.md's documented CAUSE workflow (est_cause_params -> filter sig SNPs -> cause()) with 147 sig SNPs (above the stated >=100 floor) crashes inside cause():::in_sample_elpd_loo() with 'non-numeric argument to binary operator', reproducible at both 2,000 and 30,000 background variants.
recommendations.root_cause: cause 1.2.0.335's in_sample_elpd_loo() calls loo_compare() and indexes its return value assuming a shape that the installed loo 2.10.1 no longer produces -- a package-version incompatibility, not a coding error in any file this Skill ships.
recommendations.fix: Add a version-pinning note to SKILL.md's CAUSE section (e.g. 'verified against cause X.Y + loo Z.W; if cause() crashes inside in_sample_elpd_loo, check for a loo_compare() return-shape mismatch') so an agent hitting this doesn't mistake it for its own error.

recommendations.title: qhet_mvmr fallback is not reliable at very low conditional F, and SKILL.md does not say so
recommendations.problem: When conditional F dropped below 1 (a more extreme but plausible correlated-exposure scenario than the pre-fix audit's condF~2.7), qhet_mvmr's point estimate diverged substantially from both MVMR-IVW and planted truth, including a sign flip on the second exposure.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's MVMR section describes qhet_mvmr as 'robust to weak conditional instruments' without a lower floor; the Q-minimization estimator itself is not immune to sufficiently weak conditional instruments.
recommendations.fix: Add a caveat to the MVMR section: qhet_mvmr improves on IVW at moderately low conditional F (5-10) but is not validated below approximately F=2-3; below that, flag the analysis as underpowered rather than reporting a point estimate.

recommendations.title: Steiger directionality test silently returns NULL under SKILL.md's own inline code (carried over, not part of this fix round)
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'Bidirectional and Steiger' inline code block never sets samplesize.exposure/samplesize.outcome, so directionality_test() returns NULL with only a printed message, not an error -- an agent following the snippet verbatim gets silent non-output.
recommendations.root_cause: This gap was identified in the pre-fix audit (Input 5) but was not among the findings dispatched to this fix round.
recommendations.fix: Add samplesize_col to the read_exposure_data/read_outcome_data calls in the 'Bidirectional and Steiger' section, matching the pattern already used correctly elsewhere in SKILL.md (e.g. the TwoSampleMR Standard Workflow section).
